weapons.introduction: On Athas, weapons are commonly fashioned from bone, wood, stone, obsidian, and other materials scavenged from the dying world. Metal weapons are extraordinarily rare and valuable. Standard D&D weapon damage represents common bone or wooden construction.

materials.name: Obsidian
materials.special: On a natural 1 when attacking with an obsidian weapon, the weapon breaks after the attack.

materials.name: Stone
materials.special: Heavy and difficult to wield accurately.

materials.name: Steel
materials.special: On a natural 20 with a melee weapon attack, the steel weapon breaks the opponent's equipped bone, wooden, obsidian, or stone weapon if the weapons make contact. Magical weapons are unaffected.

breakageRules.title: Obsidian Breakage
breakageRules.description: A natural 1 on an attack roll with an obsidian weapon causes the weapon to break after that attack.

breakageRules.title: Steel Shattering Strike
breakageRules.description: When a steel melee weapon scores a natural 20, it can shatter an opponent's equipped bone, wooden, obsidian, or stone weapon if the weapons make contact. This does not affect metal or magical weapons.

armor.introduction: Most armor on Athas is constructed from hide, leather, bone, chitin, and other natural materials. Iron and steel armor provide better protection, but their extraordinary expense places them beyond the reach of nearly everyone.

categories.name: Light Armor
categories.description: Flexible protection designed for mobility and comfort in the desert.

items.name: Studded Leather
items.construction: Leather reinforced with bone or chitin

categories.name: Medium Armor
categories.description: A balance of protection and mobility, commonly constructed from layered hide, bone, or chitin.

categories.name: Heavy Armor
categories.description: Substantial protection that comes with serious weight and heat considerations.

rules.title: Material Bonuses
rules.description: Iron and steel armor add +1 to the normal Armor Class calculation. Material bonuses do not stack with one another.

rules.title: Armor Durability
rules.description: Armor does not ordinarily break from normal attacks. Specific monster abilities, extraordinary attacks, or environmental hazards may damage equipment.

rules.title: Heat and Exhaustion
rules.description: Heavy armor can increase the risk of exhaustion during prolonged travel under the Athasian sun. Metal heavy armor is especially dangerous in extreme heat. Exact survival mechanics will be finalized separately.

rules.title: Oversized Equipment
rules.description: Half-giants require appropriately sized armor and equipment. The cost and availability of such items will be determined by the campaign's equipment rules.

metal.title: The Wealth of Kings
metal.tagline: On Athas, a blade of iron can be worth more than a human life.
metal.introduction: Metal is among the most valuable resources in the world of Athas. Most inhabitants of the Tablelands will live and die without ever owning a true metal weapon. A simple iron dagger may command a price comparable to that of a trained gladiator sold at auction. For an ordinary laborer, such an object represents more wealth than they could reasonably hope to earn in a lifetime.

facts.title: Metal Is Wealth
facts.description: A single metal weapon may be worth more than everything an ordinary family owns.

facts.title: Metal Attracts Attention
facts.description: Carrying an iron or steel weapon openly advertises extraordinary wealth and may attract thieves, officials, merchants, and criminals.

facts.title: Metal Is Power
facts.description: Metal weapons provide significant combat advantages over common weapons fashioned from bone, wood, and stone.

facts.title: Metal Is Dangerous to Possess
facts.description: An adventurer displaying valuable metal equipment may be questioned about its ownership, targeted for robbery, or accused of theft.
